title: Sixth and last stale-suite draw the governed-risk ranking can supply: twelve suites, three of them red, and one green suite that a mutation proved is not load-bearing

scope.drawnFrom: governedRiskFiles from scripts/quality/test-ci-coverage-census.mjs re-derived at this base, rows with untriaged true and covered false, band before score before path
scope.whyTwelveAndNotTwenty: The pool at this base is 26 files. Excluding by exact path the 85 distinct paths already judged in the five committed records leaves 12, and every one is band high, score 10, signal tenant_scoped_read, so the order is path order and nothing else. The item predicted this list exactly and it reproduced exactly, which is why this draw took it as filed rather than re-deriving a different twelve.
scope.correctionToTheClaimLine: This run's claim line said 14 of the 26 were band critical. That is WRONG and is corrected here rather than restamped: the 26 split 3 critical / 23 high, and it is 14 rows — 3 critical and 11 high — that are excluded because a prior record already judged them. The 14 is a real number attached to the wrong property.
scope.disjointnessIsAsserted: src/__tests__/behaviors/t475-stale-suite-triage-record.test.ts reads all five sibling records and fails if any path appears in two.

jestEvidence.how: Each of the twelve was executed on its own with npx jest --runTestsByPath <path> --no-coverage --ci --json --outputFile, and every count in suites[] is read out of that run's JSON by a script rather than typed.
jestEvidence.executedAt: 2026-09-24T07:42:45Z to 2026-09-24T07:42:54Z, before any verdict below was written
jestEvidence.harnessFoundTests: Asserted rather than assumed: every one of the twelve runs reports numTotalTestSuites 1, exactly one entry in testResults, and numTotalTests greater than zero. A run that matched no file would report zero, and a green exit code hides that.

mutationEvidence.why: The acceptance requires a green suite to be mutation-checked before it is credited, because green is not the same as load-bearing. Each of the nine green suites had one behaviour-changing edit applied to the product module it imports, was re-run, and the edit was reverted with the tree verified clean afterwards. Red suites were not mutated: their failure is already the measurement.
mutationEvidence.escapeIsNotCreditedAsProof: The one escape is src/lib/source/contract-evidence/__tests__/persistence.test.ts and it carries verdict repair, not wire_into_ci. The guard beside this record enforces that rule so a future edit cannot quietly promote it.
mutationEvidence.noOpMutationsRuledOut: The escape was proven to be a real behaviour change rather than a no-op edit: a throwaway probe built the payload under the mutation and printed the row-level tenant_key as the injected constant while the manifest still carried the fixture's own tenant key. A no-op mutation reads exactly like a coverage gap, and this one is not a no-op.

riskAttribution.question: The item asks the honest next question: is the governed-risk ranking exhausted because the work is done, or because the classifier is narrow? Both halves are measured here rather than asserted.
riskAttribution.howMeasured: scripts/quality/test-ci-coverage-census.mjs computes governedRiskForDirectory(root, testFiles, catalogPaths) over ALL test files in a directory, so a file inherits its directory's band. This record calls that same exported function twice per row — once with the directory's file list, once with the single file — so the two numbers come from one implementation and not from a second copy of the rule.
riskAttribution.whatThatMeans: Half this draw was ranked high because a neighbour in the same directory imports a tenant-scoped source, not because the file does. Directory grain can only inflate a file's band, never deflate it, so the ranking over-attributes at file level and the phrase 'twelve highest-risk untriaged suites' should be read as 'twelve suites in the highest-risk untriaged directories'.
riskAttribution.theAnswer: The ranking is not exhausted because the debt is retired. It is exhausted because it can only rank files in the 12 of 192 directories it assigns any signal to — 6.4% of the untriaged unrun population. 180 directories carry no signal at all, and this measurement cannot tell whether that is because they are genuinely low risk or because their imports do not resolve to a source the three regexes match. Distinguishing those two needs the census to publish a resolved-product-source count per directory, which is a change to its output shape and is filed as T-758 rather than made here.

drawConcentration.whyItMatters: The pool is one band and one score, so ranking collapses to path order and the draw becomes an alphabetical sweep. Unlike T-742, which landed nineteen of twenty in a single directory, this draw spreads across six directories in three product areas — the data plane, enterprise context, and Source contract and candidate-supplier repositories. That is not an improvement in the draw rule; it is what the remaining tail happened to contain, and a reader should not read it as coverage of those areas.

forbiddenEdits: No file judged in suites[] is edited by this item. The triage records a verdict and hands it on; wiring, rewriting and repair are the follow-on items' work. The mutations above were applied, measured and reverted, and the tree was verified clean with git status before anything was written.

followOnItems.T-754: Wire the eight credited suites into a CI job, proven by the wiring mutation the five prior draws used: replacing the new workflow step with `echo skipped` must move the census's workflow-reached count by exactly eight.
followOnItems.T-755: Assert the per-row tenant fence in the contract-evidence persistence payload, then credit and wire the suite. The escape is recorded above with its probe.
followOnItems.T-756: Re-baseline the two stale expectations and wire both suites: the intelligence-read-model composite case against #7795, which deliberately separated configuration items from applications and services and renamed the copy; and the contract-evidence templates family list against e38e5b4f5, which added an application_inventory family to the AMS pack. Neither is a product defect and neither may be deleted to make a count fall.
followOnItems.T-757: Decide the fate of src/lib/enterprise-context/derived-enterprise-read.ts — retire it or re-wire it against a canonical dataset — and update its suite to whichever is chosen. Two suites still carry a jest.mock of this module although nothing imports it at runtime, so those mocks are vestigial and should go with it.
followOnItems.T-758: Publish a resolved-product-source count per directory in the census so an unclassified directory can be told apart from one whose imports the resolver could not follow. 180 of 192 directories holding untriaged unrun suites carry no governed-risk signal, and today nothing distinguishes 'low risk' from 'invisible'.
followOnItems.T-759: A behavioural suite writes a real test file into src/lib/agent/__tests__/ mid-run and deletes it in a finally block; four suites that enumerate and then read every test file under src/ race against it. Found while baselining this draw, not looked for.
followOnItems.T-760: The census drift check exists as an npm script and runs in no workflow. The committed census is the input that decides which directory is triaged next, and it is stale by eleven files at this base with nothing failing.

T-759.what: src/__tests__/behaviors is CI-gated and is non-deterministically red. src/__tests__/behaviors/t743-agent-tests-directory-ci.test.ts deliberately writes src/lib/agent/__tests__/t743-coverage-probe.generated.test.ts during its run — that is its point, it proves the workflow reaches a file it has never heard of — and removes it in a finally block. Four suites enumerate every test file under src/ and then read each one, directly or by spawning the census, and observe the file between its creation and its deletion: test-success-guard-assertions, rendered-ai-controls-ci-coverage, liability-product-truth-ci-coverage and admin-source-action-route-suite-ci-coverage. They fail with ENOENT naming that exact path.
T-759.measured: Warm jest cache: 0 of 114 suites failed, four runs out of four. Cold cache (npx jest --clearCache first): 4, 4 and 3 suites failed in three runs out of three, every failure naming the probe file. The count moves between runs, which is what distinguishes a race from a broken assertion. This is pre-existing and was measured on a tree reverted to origin/main, not on this change.
T-759.whyItIsNotFixedHere: It is a different item in a file this claim does not hold, and the fix is a design choice — give the probe its own temporary directory, or make the four readers tolerate a file that disappears — which should be made once for all of them rather than guessed here.

T-760.what: scripts/quality/test-ci-coverage-census.mjs --check reports drift between the committed census and the measured one, and no workflow runs it. At this base the committed file is stale: testFiles 2409 against 2420 measured, coveredTestFiles 1954 against 1964.
T-760.whyItMatters: Every stale-suite draw, including this one, is ranked from that census. The item that opened this draw already warned a taker to re-derive it rather than trust the snapshot, which is a rule a person must remember. A gate would not need remembering.
T-760.whyItIsNotFixedHere: Refreshing the committed census mid-flight changes the ranking input other agents are drawing from, and wiring the check is a workflow change outside this claim.

vacuousControlsDeclared.sourceTextScanner: VACUOUS for this draw. Not one of the twelve reads a source file as text — every row scores zero for readFileSync and readFile — so the control that forbids wiring a source-text scanner never fires here. The RULE is kept in full because a future draw will need it; what is removed is the non-empty precondition T-556 attached to it, which would turn a clean draw red for being clean.
vacuousControlsDeclared.redSuites: NOT VACUOUS for this draw, and this is the first draw since T-472 where it is not. Three of the twelve are red and the control that forbids a pass-assuming verdict on a non-green suite fires on all three. The declaration is kept in the same shape as T-742's so the two records can be read side by side.

It also pins that upsert uploads are unconditional while non-upsert uploads carry ifNoneMatch, which is the difference between overwriting a tenant artifact and refusing to.

suites.rationale: Red, and stale rather than a finding about today's code. All three cases load a tenant's V4 derived enterprise read from datasets/<tenant>-synthetic-v4/derived-intelligence/enterprise-reads.json; every one of those dataset roots was deleted deliberately by #4767 (4a7ebcd85, 2026-07-13) when the canonical tenant input standard replaced them. getDerivedEnterpriseReadForTenant therefore returns null for every tenant and has done for 73 days. The suite must be updated to the contract that is actually true — the loader fails closed and returns null when its dataset is absent — with that reason recorded. The larger question belongs to the owner item, not here: the module's three exports have no runtime caller left in src/ or scripts/ (only two type-only imports in src/lib/atlas), so this is retire-or-rewire, which is a decision.

mutationCheck.notApplicable: The suite is red. Its failure is the measurement; a mutation would add nothing.

suites.rationale: Red, and the item this draw was taken under would have had it repaired as a live defect. It is stale, and the proof is inside the same file. One case of 27 fails: a composite fixture from #3298 (6758dc044, 2026-06-08) expects '2 systems/services loaded' from a cmdb_application plus a configuration_item. Eleven weeks later #7795 (8fe274ed8, 2026-09-18) — the alias-counting change — deliberately separated the two and renamed the copy, and it added a case asserting exactly the opposite, 'does not count a configuration item as an application or service', which passes today. Two cases in one file now contradict each other and the later, deliberate one is right. #7795 also added an 18-row it.each table, one per documented alias pair, and all eighteen are green, so the 'a test per aliased pair' half of backlog item 9 is met. Re-baseline the composite case against #7795 rather than editing one string: it fails at its first assertion, so the expectations after it are unverified. Nothing caught this for six days because the suite runs in no CI job.

mutationCheck.notApplicable: The suite is red. Its failure is the measurement, and the measurement is that the expectation is behind the product.

suites.rationale: Green, and NOT credited, because the mutation check found a real escape rather than confirming the suite. Replacing the per-row tenant_key in toStructuredRows() with a constant leaves all three cases passing: the probe run under the mutation shows every structured evidence row carrying the injected constant while the manifest still carries the fixture's own tenant key, so the mutation changed behaviour and the suite did not see it. The manifest's own fence IS asserted — the same substitution at the manifest fails one case — so the gap is exactly the row level, which is the level that reaches the evidence table. The suite is worth wiring once it asserts the row fence; wiring it first would credit a tenant control that is not tested.

mutationCheck.applied: The per-row tenant_key in toStructuredRows() is replaced with a constant, and separately the manifest tenant_key is replaced with the same constant.

mutationCheck.escape: Row-level fence: 0 of 3 cases failed. Manifest-level fence (control mutation, same substitution one level up): 1 of 3 cases failed, so the suite is not blind in general.
